results.name: oaks are about three tiles wide and carry half the old pixels (≤ 2400 px, ≤ 10 colours, ≤ 72 px tall)
every tree is posterised to a handful of tones (≤ 10 colours) and pines/birches stay slim
shrubs and ferns are small and simple (≤ 450 px)
canopy tone changes between neighbouring pixels stay low (≤ 19% including the outline and the rim of every leaf clump; the old noisy art was 21-40%)
shadow field is soft: the biggest step between neighbouring pixels is small (≤ 0.22; a dithered edge jumps by 0.55-1)
no isolated shadow specks, and the long (evening) shade is no more than ~1.6x the noon shade
a calm still scene changes under 1.5% of its pixels per quarter second (the fire and breeze only)
pond rows agree with their neighbours (no striping; ≤ 6% of pixels differ sharply from the row above)
night still runs at 240 game-min per real-min; midday runs at about 93
spring daylight lasts about 8 real minutes (420-540 s) and a whole day about 11
every season keeps its own light: summer longest, winter shortest, all at least 4 minutes
walking energy still follows game time (1 energy per game hour), so a slower day does not change the economy
